decisions.decision: The ragged-table gate's archive dependency was FIXED now rather than roadmapped.
decisions.rationale: Owner chose fix-now when the alternative was documenting a third instance. The gate is one report() over a loop, so removing the archive target could not move the emitted-check count, and 9 shipped files carry pipe tables so the anti-vacuity leg still held. Closing the class beat patching its next instance.

decisions.decision: The archive left the gate's SCOPE entirely; it was NOT conditionally skipped.
decisions.rationale: An existsSync skip or try/catch-and-continue would have been fail-open, which is forbidden here. A region-scoped shape pin (existsSync 0, try 1, continue 1, report 1) proves the one legitimate per-file read guard survived untouched while any added tolerance is caught.

decisions.rationale: The brief named ROADMAP.md and also forbade inventing a section; ROADMAP.md has no deferred section. FUT-04 is labelled carried from 0.0.2, which proves that register SURVIVES a milestone close -- the exact property .planning/research/ lacks, and the whole subject of this task.

decisions.decision: Superseded instructions are ANNOTATED, never rewritten or deleted.
decisions.rationale: Deleting destroys the trail that explains why the defect existed. Two legs enforce the pair in opposite directions: one asserts the original text survives verbatim, the other asserts the annotation is present. A rewrite-instead-of-annotate passes the second alone and is caught by the first.

decisions.decision: Findings were STRENGTHENED rather than relabelled when a claim outran its coverage.
decisions.rationale: When the plan's conventions claimed scope invariants were asserted in every task's verify and one task lacked them, the legs were added so the claim became true, rather than hedging the sentence. Follows the house precedent from the prior round's findings 11a-c.

decisions.decision: An over-claim was fixed at BOTH the copy and its upstream source, twice.
decisions.rationale: The roster rename-blindness contradiction and the row-guards mirroring over-claim each existed in a checker comment AND in a document that inherited it. Fixing only the document leaves the source free to re-seed the defect for the next reader.

decisions.decision: No ordinal was asserted for the signature-defect instance count.
decisions.rationale: The prior checkpoint records six consecutive ROUNDS, which counts completed rounds; whether a new sighting is a seventh instance or a fresh sighting of one already inside those six is not resolvable from the record. An unverifiable ordinal in a document about claims outrunning evidence would be self-undermining, and nothing depends on the number.

context_notes: THE LESSON THIS SESSION SHARPENED IS ABOUT WHICH GATE CATCHES WHICH DEFECT, AND IT IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. gsd-verifier returned passed at 12/12 and an unprimed content reviewer returned NEEDS WORK on the SAME artifacts at the SAME HEAD, and BOTH were correct: the verifier checked that entries EXIST, the reviewer checked whether their content is TRUE. Neither is redundant and neither substitutes for the other. Run both, and run the content review UNPRIMED -- a reviewer told what was already found confirms it and misses what is inside it. The second unprimed review then caught a false claim that the FIRST review's own remediation had introduced. ELEVEN-PLUS defects were caught before any of this shipped, and the most reliable predictor of where the next one lands is: inside the previous repair. Three of them were mine -- a guard I ordered that anchored only one of two arms, a leg I ordered that enforced an addition but not the matching removal, and a wrong diagnosis of an rg false negative. Every one was caught by the agent RECEIVING the fix, never by the one proposing it, which is the argument for keeping propose and apply adversarially split. THE GENERALISATION WORTH CARRYING: when a requirement is 'replace X with Y', a leg asserting Y exists is NOT coverage -- assert X is gone AND Y is present, because an executor can always satisfy an addition by appending. THREE DISTINCT FALSE-NEGATIVE MECHANISMS all produced the same confident zero: ripgrep's hidden-directory skip over dot-prefixed .claude/ (and --no-ignore alone does NOT fix it -- only --hidden does, measured, because git check-ignore reports those files as NOT ignored), line-oriented matching against a phrase that wraps, and a phrase wrapping across a // comment prefix so a whitespace class cannot match. A POSITIVE CONTROL caught all three. Never trust a zero without one. ALSO: the pause-work placeholder scan is a FALSE-POSITIVE GENERATOR in this repo -- it flagged 53 files, and the sampled matches are all the word 'placeholder' used descriptively, usually describing work that REPLACED one. Skill scaffolds have placeholder markers here, so the word is domain vocabulary. Do not treat that scan's output as incomplete work without reading the matches. FINALLY, a small mislabel worth knowing: there are TWO extract-samples.mjs, in lz-red-workspace (8 modules, RED-SAMPLES) and lz-refactor-workspace (259 modules, FWL-04). A gate row reported 259 for a task touching the lz-red tree. Both were green so nothing broke, but name the workspace, not just the script.
